caption:
Gallup's latest India report puts it plainly: 59% of employees say they aren't heard. Not lazy. Not checked out. Unheard.

That is not an engagement problem. It is a command problem.

In 35 years of military command, I watched capable officers get overlooked for one reason — their delivery did not match their competence. The work was sound. The room never registered it.

The fix is mechanical, not emotional. Bearing before you speak. Tone that stays level when the stakes rise. Calculated silence instead of filling every gap. You hold the floor by being steady, not by being louder.

If your idea only lands when someone else repeats it, the idea was never the issue. The transmission was.

— Colonel Suhag

topic.title: Gallup: 59% of Indian employees unheard, not disengaged
topic.angle: Lumina's audience is exactly the competent operator on the wrong side of Gallup's clarity-and-communication gap — delivering, but not landing in the room.
topic.why_now: Gallup's State of the Global Workplace: 2026 landed ~18 days ago and its India companion report ~24 days ago, making them the current reference point for Indian HR and leadership commentary for the next 2–3 weeks.

rationale: A stark, text-only stat card matches the brand's plainspoken authority and lets the Gallup figure carry the weight without decoration.
